promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Effects of exercise and physical training

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of the skeletal system?
questions.explain: Red and white blood cells are produced in the bone marrow of certain bones.

questions.q: The femur is an example of which type of bone?
questions.explain: Long bones such as the femur act as levers to create large ranges of movement.

questions.q: Which of the following is a ball and socket joint?
questions.explain: The hip is a ball and socket joint allowing movement in many directions.

questions.q: What is the role of a tendon?
options: To cushion the ends of bones
questions.explain: Tendons attach muscle to bone, while ligaments connect bone to bone.

questions.q: Which muscle is located at the back of the upper arm?
questions.explain: The triceps sit at the rear of the upper arm and extend the elbow.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explain: The heart has two atria and two ventricles, giving four chambers.

questions.q: Where does gaseous exchange take place in the lungs?
questions.explain: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged across the thin walls of the alveoli.

questions.q: Which formula correctly shows how cardiac output is calculated?
options: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate
Cardiac output = heart rate ÷ stroke volume
Cardiac output = stroke volume + heart rate
Cardiac output = tidal volume × breathing rate
questions.explain: Cardiac output equals the volume pumped per beat multiplied by beats per minute.

questions.q: The elbow is a hinge joint. Which pair of movements does it allow?
questions.explain: A hinge joint like the elbow permits movement in one plane: flexion and extension.

questions.q: During the upward (lifting) phase of a biceps curl, what role does the biceps perform?
questions.explain: The biceps contracts as the agonist while the triceps relaxes as the antagonist.

questions.q: In an isometric contraction, what happens to the length of the muscle?
questions.explain: In an isometric contraction the muscle produces tension without changing length, as in a plank.

questions.q: Which type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, usually under high pressure.

questions.q: During exercise, which process reduces blood flow to the digestive system so more blood reaches the working muscles?
questions.explain: Vasoconstriction narrows vessels to organs like the gut, redirecting blood to muscles (vascular shunting).

questions.q: What is meant by tidal volume?
options: The volume of air breathed in or out during one normal breath
The maximum volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled
The number of breaths taken each minute
The air remaining in the lungs after full exhalation
questions.explain: Tidal volume is the amount of air moved per breath during normal, resting breathing.

questions.q: What happens to the diaphragm during inspiration (breathing in)?
questions.explain: During inspiration the diaphragm contracts and flattens, increasing chest volume and drawing air in.

questions.q: Which of the following is a long-term effect of aerobic training on the heart?
options: Cardiac hypertrophy (the heart muscle grows larger and stronger)
A permanently raised resting heart rate
A reduction in the number of heart chambers
A permanent increase in blood pressure at rest
questions.explain: Regular aerobic training enlarges and strengthens the heart, increasing stroke volume.

questions.q: An athlete has a stroke volume of 70 ml and a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. What is their cardiac output?
questions.explain: Cardiac output = 70 ml × 80 bpm = 5600 ml/min.

questions.q: As a footballer straightens their leg to kick the ball, what movement occurs at the knee joint?
questions.explain: Straightening the leg increases the angle at the knee, which is extension.

questions.q: After several months of regular resistance training, a person's biceps become noticeably larger. Which adaptation explains this?
questions.explain: Resistance training over time increases muscle size, known as muscle hypertrophy.

questions.q: A trained endurance runner has a resting heart rate of 45 bpm, compared with 72 bpm for an untrained person. This lower resting rate is mainly because their heart...
options: pumps more blood per beat (increased stroke volume)
can no longer speed up during exercise
questions.explain: A stronger, larger heart ejects more blood per beat, so fewer beats are needed at rest (bradycardia).

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) PE & Sport Science (J587) specification; Applied Anatomy and Physiology
